prompt: What does each line of git log --oneline show?
hint: Two things, from left to right.

choices.text: The files the commit changed, and how many lines
choices.why: That is what --stat adds. The one-line form leaves it out.

choices.text: A short id and the first line of the message
choices.why: Right. That first line is the only part most people read.

choices.text: The author and the date
choices.why: The full format shows those. --oneline drops them.

choices.text: The branch and the number of the commit
choices.why: Commits have no numbers, only ids computed from their content.

prompt: HEAD is the commit you are on. What is HEAD~3?
hint: Follow parent.

choices.text: The third commit of the repository
choices.why: ~ counts back from HEAD, not forward from the start.

choices.text: The commit three before HEAD
choices.why: Right. Its parent's parent's parent.

choices.text: The last three commits, taken together
choices.why: It names one commit. A range needs two names.

choices.text: A commit that is three days old
choices.why: The number counts commits, not days.

prompt: Match each option of git log to the commits it keeps.
hint: One description is not a git log filter.

pairs.right: Commits made on or after that date

prompt: git log --grep=price listed "Put the prices up for September". Why did a search for price find prices?
hint: It is not looking for a whole word.

choices.text: Git ignores the letter s at the end of words
choices.why: It knows nothing about English plurals. prices simply contains price.

choices.text: It matched the files, not the message
choices.why: --grep searches messages only. The files are what -S searches.

choices.text: It matches a pattern, not a word
choices.why: Right. price is inside prices, so it matches.

choices.text: Bruno tagged the commit with the word price
choices.why: There are no tags here. The match is on the message text itself.

prompt: Every commit Bruno made to menu.html: git log --oneline --author=Bruno ___ menu.html
hint: What separates options from file names.

prompt: A diff has the line @@ -1,3 +1,3 @@. What does it say?
hint: Old side, then new side.

choices.text: Three lines were removed and three added
choices.why: The counts are the size of the hunk on each side, context included.

choices.text: It is the first of three hunks
choices.why: Nothing in the header counts hunks.

choices.text: Lines 1 to 3 of each side are shown
choices.why: Right. From line 1, three lines, in the old file and in the new one.

choices.text: The file changed in commits 1 and 3
choices.why: A diff compares two snapshots. It names no commits in its hunks.

prompt: Match what starts a line of a diff to what the line is.
hint: One description is not something a diff line can be.

pairs.right: A line only on the old side
A line only on the new side

right_distractors: A line that was changed in place

prompt: Match each command to what it compares.
hint: The figure had one bracket per command.

pairs.right: The staging area and the working tree
The last commit and the staging area

right_distractors: Your copy and the shared server's

prompt: Three commits separate HEAD~3 from HEAD: rye removed, cheese rolls added, a link added. What does git diff HEAD~3 HEAD -- menu.html show?
hint: A diff compares two snapshots.

choices.text: Three hunks, one for each commit
choices.why: Hunks are places in the file, not commits. The diff knows nothing of the steps.

choices.text: The two ends only, with no trace of the steps
choices.why: Right. It is the difference between the two ends, and the link is in another file anyway.

choices.text: Only the last commit's change, since HEAD comes last
choices.why: Naming two commits compares both ends; all three commits' changes are in it.

choices.text: The link to the menu, and the two menu changes
choices.why: -- menu.html limits it to that file, and the link was added to index.html.

prompt: In a diff, how does a line whose price changed from 2.50 to 2.80 appear?
hint: A diff has no symbol for changed.

choices.text: As one line marked with a ~
choices.why: There is no ~ in a diff. A changed line is two lines.

choices.text: As the old line with - and the new line with +
choices.why: Right. Removed and added, one after the other.

choices.text: As a context line, since the rest of it is the same
choices.why: Context lines are unchanged ones. This one changed.

choices.text: Only with +, since the old price is gone
choices.why: The old version is shown too, with -, so you can see what it was.

prompt: What does git show 1b2d576 print?
hint: It is one commit, whole.

choices.text: Its log entry, then its diff
choices.why: Right. The who, when and why, then what changed.

choices.text: Every file of the project as it was then
choices.why: That is the snapshot. show prints the change, or one file if you name it.

choices.text: The commits made after it
choices.why: That is a log question. show is about one commit.

choices.text: Only its message
choices.why: The message is there, and so is the diff below it.

prompt: What does git show HEAD~3:menu.html do?
hint: Nothing on the disk changes.

choices.text: Restores menu.html to that version
choices.why: show only prints. Bringing a version back is lesson 4.

choices.text: Prints the changes made to menu.html since then
choices.why: That would be a diff. The colon form prints the file itself.

choices.text: Lists the three commits that changed menu.html
choices.why: That is git log -- menu.html.

choices.text: Prints menu.html as it was three commits ago
choices.why: Right. The file from that snapshot, printed to the screen.

prompt: What is git blame for, day to day?
hint: It leads to a commit, and a commit has a message.

choices.text: Counting how many bugs each person wrote
choices.why: It knows nothing about bugs. It knows which commit last touched each line.

choices.text: The commit behind a line, and its why
choices.why: Right. The name is unfortunate; the use is finding the explanation.

choices.text: Locking a line so nobody else can change it
choices.why: Git has no locks. blame only reads.

choices.text: Showing who first created the file
choices.why: It shows who last changed each line, which is often somebody else.

prompt: git blame shows line 2 of menu.html as 1b2d5761 (Bruno Lima 2026-09-16). Ana wrote that line on the 14th. Why does blame name Bruno?
hint: blame names the last commit to touch a line.

choices.text: His commit was the last to touch it
choices.why: Right. He changed its price. blame shows the latest change; the log or show of earlier commits has the rest.

choices.text: Bruno was the one who committed the whole file
choices.why: Ana added the file. blame works per line, not per file.

choices.text: Blame credits whoever reviewed a line
choices.why: Git records no reviews. It records authors of commits.

choices.text: The author was copied from the previous line
choices.why: Line 1 is Ana's. Each line is looked up on its own.

prompt: Rye bread is no longer on the menu, and Ana wants to know when and why it went. Which command answers that?
hint: The line does not exist any more.

choices.text: git blame -L 1,3 menu.html
choices.why: blame only sees lines that are there now, and the rye line is not.

choices.text: git log -S "Rye" --oneline
choices.why: Right. It lists the commits that added or removed the text, and the removal has the reason.

choices.text: git log --oneline --grep=Rye
choices.why: That searches messages, and the removal's message says rye in lower case. -S searches the content.

choices.text: git show HEAD:menu.html
choices.why: That prints today's menu, where rye is already missing.

prompt: To list the commits that added or removed the text Rye: git log ___ "Rye"
hint: The pickaxe.

prompt: A price on the menu looks wrong. Put these steps in the order you would take them.
hint: From the line to the reason.
items: Run git blame on the file to find the line's commit
Run git show on that commit
Read the message and the diff to see why it changed
Ask the author, if the message does not explain it
trap: Asking comes last: the commit usually already says why.

prompt: Match each question to the command that answers it.
hint: One command on the right answers none of them.

pairs.left: What did Bruno change this week?
What exactly is different from the last commit?
What did menu.html say on Wednesday?

prompt: Which of these are true of git diff? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two are the belief lesson 1 corrected.

choices.text: It is computed when you ask, from two snapshots
choices.why: Yes. No diff is stored; commits hold snapshots.

choices.text: It reads the diffs Git stored at each commit
choices.why: Git stores snapshots, and works the diff out.

choices.text: With no arguments it compares the staging area and the working tree
choices.why: Yes. That is why it showed only the unstaged price edit.

choices.text: Between two commits it lists each commit in between
choices.why: It compares the two ends and says nothing about the steps.

choices.text: A changed line appears as a - line and a + line
choices.why: Yes. There is no separate mark for a change.

prompt: Ana wants to see the September price change: who made it, why, and exactly which lines. She knows its id, 1b2d576. What is the one command?
hint: Log entry and diff, together.

choices.text: git log 1b2d576
choices.why: That lists the commit and everything before it, without the diff.

choices.text: git blame 1b2d576
choices.why: blame takes a file, not a commit, and shows lines rather than a change.

choices.text: git diff 1b2d576
choices.why: That compares that commit with your working tree today, and has no message.

choices.text: git show 1b2d576
choices.why: Right. The author, date and message, then the diff against its parent.
